evals.prompt: I need a rate limiter for our API, in Python. Sliding window — each client id gets max 100 requests per 60-second window. It should be possible to swap out the clock for testing. We use pytest. Build it in this directory.
evals.expected_output: A rate limiter class built test-first: tests written one at a time with spec-like names, clock injected as a dependency (not instantiated inside), full pytest suite passing. Autonomous-mode fallback should kick in (no user available to interview) with assumptions stated.
assertions: The full pytest suite passes (run with the workspace venv's pytest)
The rate limiter receives its clock as an injected dependency (constructor or parameter) instead of calling time.time()/monotonic() directly inside the limiter logic
Tests control time through a fake/stub clock — no time.sleep() appears anywhere in the tests
Sliding-window behavior is actually specified by the tests: the 101st request inside a window is rejected, and capacity frees up once old requests age out of the 60s window
Test names read like behavior specifications (describe outcomes, not implementation)
Work was done on a tdd/<slug> working branch, not directly on main
The SUMMARY.md shows a test-first chronology (each behavior's test written and seen failing before its implementation) and states the assumptions made instead of asking questions

evals.prompt: This report_generator.py has been running in production since 2023 and has zero tests. I need it to also support CSV output (same data, comma-separated, with a header row) so finance can import it. Please don't break the existing text report — other systems parse it.
evals.expected_output: Characterization tests pinning current text-report behavior (including quirks like int truncation and skipped-row counting) are written BEFORE any change; odd behaviors flagged rather than silently fixed; then CSV support added via red-green-refactor without altering existing output.
assertions: Characterization tests pinning the ORIGINAL text-report behavior were written and passing BEFORE report_generator.py was first modified (per SUMMARY.md chronology and test content)
The characterization tests capture the quirks: integer truncation of totals/averages (not rounding) and the skipped-bad-rows count in the footer
For identical input records, the final text report output is byte-identical to the original fixture's output (verified by running both)
CSV output is implemented: comma-separated rows with a header row, importable data matching the report's numbers
The truncation quirk was flagged to the user as suspicious but NOT silently changed
The full pytest suite passes (run with the workspace venv's pytest)
Work was done on a tdd/<slug> working branch, not directly on main
